decisions.reason: Correctly attributes the failure to fs-ext@2.1.1 pulled by dsh-session-persistence-jsonl, its node-gyp configure build install step, and the missing Visual Studio/MSVC toolchain, grounded in the log, manifest and README.

Explains that the top-level static flock import forces fs-ext to resolve and load even on Windows, so --ignore-scripts only moves the failure from install time to service boot and cannot yield a working service.

Correctly distinguishes the Windows named-semaphore path (CreateSemaphoreW etc.) from POSIX flock and uses the dead-code-on-Windows point to justify an import-safe stub, but the plan never ensures Linux/macOS keep the real native flock build.

Follows the node-pty patchedDependencies precedent, registers the patch in pnpm-workspace.yaml, skips node-gyp and adds an import-safe entry stub with install and boot checks; however the no-op install and entry stub are unconditional, so non-Windows loses the native module, and no allowBuilds/build-permission or flock-callback module-load check is proposed.
Explicitly avoids Visual Studio, uses the repository-managed pnpm patch mechanism, and states no upstream dependency is modified; correctly treats local patched installed files as allowed.
Cites only DSH-0.1.3-A1 and admits the suffix could not be confirmed; the full card id DSH-0.1.3-A1-03 and its connection are not established, and a bare/incomplete id earns no credit.

caps.reason: The plan explicitly refuses to install Visual Studio and relies on the patch instead.
The report explicitly rejects --ignore-scripts as a fix and provides an import-safe stub plus patch registration.
The plan uses a local repository-managed pnpm patch and explicitly avoids upstream edits; the optional lease.ts change is local source, not upstream.

The patch unconditionally disables the node-gyp build and replaces the fs-ext entry with a universal stub on all platforms, leaving POSIX flock without the real native lock implementation, which weakens genuine write ownership.
